questions.explanation: Routers use the longest prefix match to select the most specific route for a packet. This ensures that the packet is forwarded along the most appropriate path based on the destination IP address.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about Distance Vector routing?

options.text: Routers have complete knowledge of the network topology.
Routers only know the distance to their neighbors.
Convergence is fast due to frequent updates.

questions.explanation: In Distance Vector routing, routers maintain a table of minimum distances to every destination and share this information with their neighbors, but they do not have a complete view of the network topology.

questions.stem: What information do routers share in Link State routing protocols?
questions.explanation: Link State routing protocols involve routers sharing information about the entire network topology, allowing each router to independently compute the shortest path to every destination.

questions.explanation: Distance Vector routing protocols can suffer from slow convergence because updates are propagated incrementally between routers, which can delay the network's adaptation to changes.

questions.stem: Discuss the trade-offs between Distance Vector and Link State routing protocols in terms of scalability and computational resources.
